chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, from Ya'qub Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umair, from Abu al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The gift is valid whether you have taken possession or not, whether you have divided it or not; for the people intended the 'gift given before possession' (nihlah) but erred, and the 'gift given before possession' is not valid until it is taken possession of.

key_terms.النِّحْلَ: Gift given before possession (a specific legal category)
key_terms.الْهَبَةُ: Gift (general term for voluntary transfer of property)

ai.seo_question: Is a gift valid in Islam before the recipient takes possession of it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s clarification that a general gift (hibah) is legally binding upon declaration, whereas the specific pre-possession gift (nihlah) requires actual transfer of possession to be valid. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical act of taking possession (qabd) as a condition for the perfection of certain gift contracts, correcting common misconceptions about the timing of validity.
